blocks.x: Blockchain & Digital Trust applied to Maritime, Ports & Shipping. This page sets out the operating context, the delivery pattern we run, the services and platforms involved, and the outcomes we commit to.

Ports and carriers orchestrate billion-dollar physics: berth planning, crane productivity, vessel scheduling and cargo integrity. Telemetry-to-decision loops (berth windows, yard flows, maintenance) decide throughput on the same infrastructure — pure intelligence arbitrage.

items: Paper bills of lading persist; fraud and delay.
Vessel schedules vs. Yard reality disconnected; anchorage waits cost.

blocks.x: The pattern composes Blockchain Analytics & Regulatory Compliance, Decentralized Identity & Verifiable Credentials, Provenance, Traceability & Supply Chain Trust from the Blockchain & Digital Trust tower, wired into the unit's workflows (Berth/vessel planning, Yard/gate orchestration, Crane/equipment maintenance) on Dataq Ledger and Dataq Sentinel. Governance inherits the sector frame — SOLAS/ISPS among others — with evidence generated by the delivery itself.

items: On-chain transparency, operationalized: analytics, Travel Rule and MiCA-aligned controls.
Permissioned networks for multi-party truth: governance, consensus and integration done institutionally.
Instruments as tokens: issuance, custody and lifecycle under securities-law discipline.
Electronic bills with legal-grade evidence (fraud/delay down)

blocks.x: At industry level, the same pattern

At Logistics & Supply Chain level this capability reads as: shared evidence between shipper, carrier and insurer (claims and disputes collapse). The sub-industry page narrows it to the unit's workflows, regimes and KPIs.

Delivery follows the same weekly rhythm on every program of this type. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline: the current metric is measured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, not quietly extended.
